liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Tennessee Jed** (2 reviews): Reviewer calls the Tennessee Jed very hot, and also singles out Lazy Lightnin' into Supplication; Reviewer calls this an all-time Jed and a top Looks Like Rain into Supplication [16][19]
- **Row Jimmy** (2 reviews): Reviewer singles out Jerry's second lead, around 4:00 to 6:00, played on pedal steel, as the show's highlight; Reviewer says the Row Jimmy matches the best versions and is thoroughly jammed [13][19]
- **Candyman** (1 review): Reviewer praises Mission in the Rain and Candyman for their slow, laid-back 1976 feel [14]
- **The Wheel** (1 review): Reviewer loves the 1976-style introductions leading into The Wheel [14]
- **Saint Stephen** (1 review): The reviewer calls the second-set Stephen extremely relaxed and kicked-back [11]

## Setlist highlights

- **Mission In The Rain**: rare: 5 archived performances [22]

## The recordings

- **gd76-06-29.sbd.bertha.31144.sbeok.flacf** (recommended): soundboard; 23 songs; 177 min; rated 4.82/5 by 33 [1]
- **gd76-06-29.sbd.parrillo.1812.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 23 songs; 177 min; rated 4.58/5 by 36 [2]. Said about its sound: Reviewer describes the sound as crisp and deserving five stars; Reviewer gives the sound an A+, a rare top grade from them; Reviewer finds the sound quality good but not great, despite the Betty Board label [15][19][21]
- **gd1976-06-29.149860.BettyBoard.Anon.Noel.t-flac16**: soundboard; 22 songs; 177 min; rated 4.8/5 by 5 [5]
- **gd1976-06-29.sbd.bertha.ashley.86216.dvdf**: soundboard; 0 songs; 0 min [9]

## Around the show

- Reviewer says they had the first set for a couple of years before finding the second set [11]
- Reviewer hears a mostly laid-back feel, with the band playing well together, especially in the second set, and Donna occasionally singing in key [12]
- Reviewer ranks this among the top five shows of all time and says the setlist gives a sense of 1976 [13]
- Reviewer hears this as a long, trippy forerunner of what came at the Orpheum shows, noting Chicago shows had personality [16]
- Reviewer points to the 10-10-82 show as another perfect Tennessee Jed [20]
- Reviewer finds the setlist boring and says other 1976 shows are preferable to this one [21]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd76-06-29.sbd.bertha.31144.sbeok.flacf**: transferred by Jay Ashley; source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Soundboard transfer chain runs from analog PCM to DAT, CDA, SHN, then the Bertha DAW, then DVD audio and FLAC [1]
- **gd76-06-29.sbd.parrillo.1812.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [2]. Also: Reviewer has had this board on tape since the early 1980s and finds this copy much better [16]
- **gd1976-06-29.149860.BettyBoard.Anon.Noel.t-flac16**: taped by Source & Transfer by Anonymous; transferred by Edited & Mastered using Adobe Audition by Joe Noel April 10, 2020; source: Source: Betty Cantor’s SBD Reel Master > Beta tape > Beta VCR > PCM [5]. Also: Betty Board source was shared anonymously; Hollister, Tiedrich and Parrillo supplied the patch source [5]
- **gd1976-06-29.sbd.bertha.ashley.86216.dvdf**: transferred by Jay Ashley; source: Bertha Remaster of the Master Reel Betty Board source [9]. Also: Remastered in June 2005 on a custom dual-DAW nicknamed Bertha by an archive.org user [9]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Worthpoint: [THE GRATEFUL DEAD - AUDITORIUM THEATRE, CHICAGO 29TH JUNE 1976 RECORD STORE DAY! | #4849303161](https://www.worthpoint.com/worthopedia/grateful-dead-auditorium-theatre-4849303161) [23]
